The proposal side (reduce blur/animation while the machine sits idle, revert on activity) mirrors the shipped battery-saver and gaming presets' exact tool calls, so every suggested change is already a validated registry tool. rules.title: Battery drains while the machine sits idle: throttle blur/animation, revert on resume

fix.text: Deterministic idle-throttle proposal (issue #120 phase 2.3): while the machine sits idle, blur compositing and long animations are the cheapest visible power sinks. The exact reductions below are the shipped battery-saver preset's own tool calls — nothing invented. Propose them as a pair in the ledger (brain settings propose), approve when you actually walk away, and propose the revert when you are back.
Propose the throttle (dry-run preview, nothing written):
fix.command: python3 -m assistant.capabilities.brain settings propose --file ~/.config/caelestia/shell.json --call setBlurEnabled=false --call setAnimationSpeed=0.25 --reason 'idle throttle: reduce blur and animation while away'

fix.text: Propose the revert for when activity resumes (blur back on, animations back to your normal speed — 1.0 is the shipped default):
fix.command: python3 -m assistant.capabilities.brain settings propose --file ~/.config/caelestia/shell.json --call setBlurEnabled=true --call setAnimationSpeed=1.0 --reason 'idle throttle revert: activity resumed'

fix.text: Approve/reject the pending proposals with: brain ledger list, then brain ledger approve ID (approve applies through the gated applier with a backup; reject discards).
The one-shot, no-ledger equivalent is the battery-saver preset: caelestia-assist settings 'battery saver' --apply (multi-change, so it previews and asks for --confirm first).

undo.text: caelestia-assist settings --restore puts the single backup slot back, or --undo-id ID reverts one specific change from the bounded history.

rules.clarify_probe: Paste `cat /sys/class/power_supply/BAT*/capacity` before and after the idle window (a plain read) — if the drop is under ~3% the drain is not the compositor and this rule is not your answer.
